errors.english: [note: referring to a ritual source of fire or a specific lightning-fire]
errors.why: Śakra's head (śakramūrdhan) is the standard Pramāṇa example of an anthill emitting smoke-like vapour, not a ritual fire or lightning.

fix.find: [note: referring to a ritual source of fire or a specific lightning-fire]
fix.replace: [note: śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', i.e. an anthill, from which a smoke-like vapour rises]

errors.english: seemingly dissimilar causes such as heavy clay and so forth
errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung (gomaya), the classic example of a lotus-plant arising from a heterogeneous cause; it is not 'heavy clay'.

errors.english: Otherwise, there would be no purpose [note: or occurrence] at any time.
errors.why: The argument is that otherwise smoke would not occur even once (kadācid api na syāt); 'purpose' misreads the point.

note: The causal argument is followed well, but two Pramāṇa stock examples (Indra's head = anthill, cow dung) are misidentified.

errors.english: those individual pillars, which have no individual capacity to support a beam
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of those which individually cannot lift the beam (the lifters), with no mention of pillars.

note: A careful rendering of a terse lemma-commentary; the argument about the whole and recognition is followed correctly.

errors.english:
The actions of the Supreme
Sage are said to be intention and what is intended.
errors.why: MMK 17.2 (karmoktaṃ paramarṣiṇā): the Supreme Sage is the one who taught that action is intention and what is intended, not the owner of the actions.

fix.find:
The actions of the Supreme
Sage are said to be intention and what is intended.
fix.replace:
Actions, the Supreme
Sage has said, are intention and what is intended.

note: Faithful commentary rendering with correct cetanā/cetayitvā handling, apart from the root verse's agent.

span_why: The opening sentence ('If one says, "You are impure," ... it is also the very same downfall') translates the previous side's last line.

errors.english: they obtain the downfall of causing exhaustion [note: referring to a specific class of legal disputes that exhaust the community's harmony]
errors.why: ཟད་བྱེད is the name of the pāyantika for disparaging/reopening a duly completed legal act; the note invents a class of disputes.

errors.english: The learned ones have said that it is not otherwise.
errors.why: The point is that with doubt the offence is a duṣkṛta and not the other offence (the pāyantika), not 'not otherwise'.

note: Generally follows the verse Vinaya, but the reopening-of-acts section is muddled and it repeats the previous side's opening.

errors.english: then the words for the objects of other philosophical views would not engage without a cause
errors.why: The summary verses are rendered as prose, and 'without a basis' (རྒྱུ་མེད་ཅན) qualifies the groundless objects of other views, not the verb.

errors.english: Therefore, these are held to be the objects of the mind.
errors.why: The words are held to have the mental (conceptual) object as their domain; they are not themselves objects of mind.

note: Sound rendering of the apoha argument; the summary verses lose their form and their conclusion is slightly misread.

errors.english: the cause of the quarrel which is being sustained must also be expelled from the residence
errors.why: The lemma says the person who furnishes the cause of quarrels is also to be expelled, as the gloss that follows makes clear.

fix.find: the cause of the quarrel which is being sustained must also be expelled from the residence
fix.replace: one who furnishes the cause of quarrels must also be expelled from the residence

errors.english: such as the monk (Greskyé) Seyi [note: Sanskrit: Seyya]
errors.why: The Tibetan simply names the monk Gre skyes; 'Seyi' and the Sanskrit 'Seyya' are unsupported.

note: The pravāsana procedure is rendered accurately, apart from one lemma that makes the cause rather than the person the one expelled.

errors.english: Because they are the essence of what should and should not be done
errors.why: The etymology says that, being of the nature of doing and not-doing, they are karma (the first half of karmapatha); 'they are karma' is dropped.

errors.english: the instructions on relying upon the root of faith
errors.why: In context (དད་པ་བརྟན་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཐབས, དད་པ་བརྟན་པར་འདོད་པ) this is the method for stabilizing the root of faith.

note: A readable, essentially faithful rendering of the instruction on faith, with a slipped karmapatha etymology.

errors.english: The clay materials used for cleaning should be placed in earthenware shards.
errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung, the material for plastering (འདག་རྫས), not clay.

fix.find: The clay materials used for cleaning
fix.replace: The cow dung used as plastering material

errors.english: Except for the plants that do not grow, all others should be removed.
errors.why: The sentence continues སྲོགས་ཆགས་ from the previous side: it is about living creatures not arising in the old grass, not about plants.

errors.english: nor with the tasks of receiving oral transmissions, reading, chanting, yoga, or mental cultivation
errors.why: Udāyin promises the novices that they will not want for bowls, robes, etc., or for instruction, reading, recitation, yoga and attention; he is not promising to spare them these.
Udāyin had them take niśraya (formal dependence) under himself; 'settle' loses the Vinaya term.

note: The section heading and the narrative are well handled, but there are a cow-dung error and two misreadings in Udāyin's speech.

errors.english: If you say, "Even if that qualified meaning is established
errors.why: The side's opening clause (the mention of [proving the probandum] would be superfluous), which ends the previous sentence, is not translated.

note: A precise rendering of a difficult dialectical passage on sādharmya and utsarga/apavāda, with verse kept as verse.

errors.english: are viable [note: literally: "fit for a youth to eat"] and undamaged
errors.why: རུང་བར་མ་བྱས་པ is the Vinaya term 'not made allowable' (akalpikṛta), and ཁྱེའུ་ཁ་འཐོན་པ means sprouts; the 'viable' rendering and its note are wrong.

fix.find: are viable [note: literally: "fit for a youth to eat"] and undamaged
fix.replace: and sprouts have not been made allowable (akalpikṛta) and are undamaged

note: The seed classes and the offence analysis are rendered well, apart from the key 'not made allowable' condition.
